workflow.decision: Use exposed development diagnostics as a reason to reconsider deployment hygiene and overlooked artifact classes, not as proof that every interface is insecure. The remaining question is which auxiliary artifacts belong in the surface inventory.

Separate metadata-derived origin information, upstream-source availability, and file-inventory clues. An inaccessible origin leaves its cause unresolved but does not erase independently observed metadata; use the available inventory to narrow the next review question.

Use deployment inventory to identify development-only or auxiliary entries that ordinary user-facing navigation may omit. Prioritize these as candidates while carrying unresolved handler, provenance, and access-gate questions rather than treating a filename as demonstrated reachability.

tools.purpose: Extract printable filename clues from repository metadata as an initial directory-inventory aid.
tools.when: When examining an authorized metadata artifact; completeness and correspondence with deployed files remain separate questions.

handoffs.acceptance_gate: Require authorized source correspondence and either entry/gate evidence or an explicitly inferred candidate with a bounded validation question. Return missing provenance or handler questions; directory names and an inaccessible upstream repository do not constitute source recovery or reachability proof.

limitations: This is a historical CTF leaderboard incident. All vulnerability, access, and disclosure outcomes remain author reports; only article text and quotation identity were checked here.
The upstream repository was unavailable to the author. Private versus removed is explicitly speculative, not a verified explanation.
The printable-text inventory method establishes neither completeness nor deployed revision correspondence. The article does not supply a systematic handler/gate inventory or source-audit record.
The initial inference from diagnostic exposure to weak overall protection is a prioritization heuristic, not a whole-site security finding or a controlled comparison.
The article states that the vulnerabilities were fixed but supplies no assessed patch, deployment receipt, or regression coverage. Remediation is therefore unverified by this extraction.

candidate_additions.guidance: Include development and deployment artifacts in the interface inventory, not only ordinary navigation. Metadata-derived auxiliary entries remain candidates until their actor, handler, and gates are established.

Printable-text extraction can provide a preliminary artifact-name inventory from supplied metadata. Preserve acquisition provenance and label completeness, source recovery, and deployment correspondence as unresolved rather than promoting readable names to confirmed interfaces.

Accept metadata-led candidates only with authorized matching source and explicit provenance, or return the missing-source question. Carry upstream access failure as a limit instead of inventing source content, handlers, or the cause of unavailability.
